subject: Vendor enumeration, VectorDB introduction, and logging region migration
messages:
From: Tina Lopez <tina.lopez@acmesec.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: BankCorp Procurement <procurement@bankcorp.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Request: updated third-party roster & questions on new VectorDB and logging region move

Hi Naomi,

Hope you are well. BankCorp is updating our third-party dependency inventory ahead of an internal audit and we need a few clarifications on your recent notices:

- We saw a note about a new VectorDB vendor being introduced for embedding caches (VectorOp). Please confirm whether VectorOp will be used to persist any customer prompts or user PII, and where those instances will be hosted (region).
- There was also an operational notice about your logging provider moving regions. Can you confirm the migration date, which logs are in scope (access logs, full request/response, metadata only), and whether any logs will transit or be stored in the EU during/after the change?
- Please provide the latest subprocessor roster (CSV preferred), SOC 2 Type II evidence or summary, and any attestations from VectorOp. If there are separate data flow diagrams that show where embeddings and KV caches live versus persistent storage, that would help our security team sign off.

We appreciate a consolidated response and a target timeline so procurement can coordinate any contract addenda.

Thanks,
Tina Lopez
Sr. Security Compliance Manager
Acme Security (on behalf of BankCorp)

Attachments: none
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Tina Lopez <tina.lopez@acmesec.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: updated third-party roster & questions on new VectorDB and logging region move

Tina,

Thanks for the heads up. Brief answers below and I attached a consolidated roster and onboarding summary for VectorOp. Longer technical detail is coming from Priyom.

- VectorOp: will be used only as an embeddings vector store for deduped/hashed embeddings used in caching layers. We do not persist raw prompts or full request payloads to VectorOp. For hosted customers, VectorOp instances for BankCorp will be provisioned in Canada (ca-central-1). For Private deployments, customers can opt for on-prem or region-of-choice.

- Logging provider migration: the provider is moving a logging ingestion endpoint from eu-west-1 to ca-central-1. Migration window is scheduled for Aug 20-22, 2026. In-scope logs are aggregated telemetry and diagnostic logs (no full request bodies or PII). Access logs and audit trails remain written to your configured region; we will not route BankCorp production logs through EU-based storage.

- Attached: subprocessor_inventory_20260802.csv, vectorop_onboarding_summary.pdf, preliminary SOC2 supplement (summary).

Next steps: Priyom will confirm encryption/KMS behavior and Karthik will confirm key management options for customers that require HSM-backed KMS. Laura, looping you for procurement coordination.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Security & Trust (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- subprocessor_inventory_20260802.csv (CSV)
- vectorop_onboarding_summary.pdf (PDF)
- redwood-soc2-supplement-summary.pdf (PDF)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Tina Lopez <tina.lopez@acmesec.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: updated third-party roster & questions on new VectorDB and logging region move

Hi Tina, Naomi,

Quick technical points on VectorOp and caching so your engineers can validate controls:

- VectorOp usage model: ephemeral embeddings are retained only for cache TTLs (default 24h, configurable per-customer). We store hashed embedding vectors; we do not store cleartext prompt text nor user identifiers in VectorOp.
- Encryption: all data at rest in VectorOp is encrypted. For Redwood Hosted customers we use provider-managed KMS by default; for Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS or an external KMS with key wrapping.
- KV cache behavior: application prefixes are namespaced per-customer; cache evictions and retention follow policy and are not used as an audit trail. If BankCorp requires zero retention of embeddings after request completion we can implement a strict TTL policy and a purge job during the migration window.

I can share an architecture excerpt if that helps; link included below. Please tell me which artifacts you need (full DF diagram, sequence flows, encryption design).

Priyom
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Related link: https://drive.google.com/redwood/arch/embed-cache-2026
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tina Lopez <tina.lopez@acmesec.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: updated third-party roster & questions on new VectorDB and logging region move

Tina / Team,

Adding a couple of controls notes from a keys and deployment perspective:

- HSM / KMS: For customers on Redwood Private we support HSM-backed key stores and can enable key wrapping so that VectorOp or any other subprocessor only holds wrapped keys. For Hosted customers we can configure AWS KMS CMKs by request under a Managed Keys addendum.
- Audit logs: We do not forward full request/response payloads to VectorOp or to the logging provider. Audit trails for admin operations are maintained in our primary control plane and can be exported on request.
- Quantized model artifacts and compiler outputs are built offline in our build pipeline; we do not ship training data or prompt stores to VectorOp.

Attached a short matrix that maps KMS/HSM options by deployment tier. Happy to set up a technical call if you want a run-through.

Karthik
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- kms-hsm-integration-matrix.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Tina Lopez <tina.lopez@acmesec.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: BankCorp Procurement <procurement@bankcorp.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: updated third-party roster & questions on new VectorDB and logging region move

Thanks Naomi, Priyom, Karthik. Useful clarifications. A couple of follow-ups from the security review:

- BankCorp requires a signed copy or redacted extract of Redwood's latest SOC 2 Type II report. Can you provide the report or a signed summary within a week?
- We need an explicit attestation from VectorOp that they do not persist PII or cleartext prompts and confirmation of the Canadian hosting location. If VectorOp cannot provide their attestation we will need a compensating control documented.
- Please confirm the contract amendment path and DocuSign timeline so procurement can prepare.

Procurement, please coordinate directly with Laura Bennett on contract language. Laura, could you please confirm the point of contact and whether Redwood will send a DocuSign amendment for the logging-region change + VectorOp addition?

Regards,
Tina Lopez
Acme Security (for BankCorp)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Tina Lopez <tina.lopez@acmesec.com>, BankCorp Procurement <procurement@bankcorp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: updated third-party roster & questions on new VectorDB and logging region move

Tina and team,

Thanks for the follow-ups — summary and deliverables below. I will have our contracts team issue a DocuSign amendment for the VectorOp addition and the logging provider region update by EOD Aug 12, 2026; proposed signature window Aug 13-18. We expect the logging migration Aug 20-22 as noted.

Deliverables (links/attachments):
- SOC2 Type II summary (redacted) attached: SOC2-Redwood-2026-type2-summary.pdf. Full report can be shared under NDA; we can execute an NDA via DocuSign if you prefer.
- VectorOp attestation attached and hosted: vectorop-attestation.pdf and https://vectorop.ai/compliance/attestation-2026. VectorOp confirms no cleartext prompt persistence and Canadian hosting for BankCorp instances.
- Subprocessor roster attached: subprocessor_inventory_20260802.csv.
- KMS/HSM matrix attached: kms-hsm-integration-matrix.xlsx.

Proposed compensating control if BankCorp wants zero persistence: enable strict TTL + immediate purge job during the migration window; Redwood will coordinate purge and provide execution logs.

Next steps:
1) Laura Bennett to coordinate contract amendment logistics with BankCorp procurement.
2) I will have contracts open a DocuSign envelope (link below) and include SOC2 redacted summary as an enclosure.
3) Priyom will schedule a 45-minute technical call to walk your security engineers through the dataflow and KMS options — please propose slots.

DocuSign envelope (draft): https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC-2026-0897
Drive folder with artifacts: https://drive.google.com/redwood/subprocessors/2026-08-02

If you need anything sooner, loop me in.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Security & Trust (acting)
Redwood Inference
